newsitem.title: MONACO: TENNIS-SAMPRAS AND MUSTER TOPPLED IN MONTE CARLO.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS AND MUSTER TOPPLED IN MONTE CARLO.

text.p: Pete Sampras and Thomas Muster, the top two players in the world, again found how hard it is to adapt to clay as they tumbled out of the Monte Carlo Open on Tuesday.
The American world number one bowed to Sweden's Magnus Larsson 3-6 6-2 6-3 while Muster lost to Frenchman Fabrice Santoro 6-2 7-6.
Boris Becker was another big name to bid an early farewell to the first major claycourt event of the season when he went down to Italy's Renzo Furlan 1-6 6-3 7-6.
Defending champion Muster's defeat was the most surprising in that he was bidding for a record fourth victory here.
"I'm playing only at 50 percent or 60 percent of my best level. It is not enough," said Muster, once the undisputed king of clay.
Muster, who lost to another Frenchman, Cedric Pioline, last week in Barcelona, was meeting his "bete noire", Santoro having beaten him in their last two encounters.

"I knew exactly what I had to do. Play short and deep, jump to the net at every opportunity. I'm happy I was able to maintain the tactics I had decided to opt for," said Santoro, ranked 90th in the world.
The tactics worked as Santoro cruised through the first set. Muster hit back by taking a 3-1 lead in the second set but his inconsistency forced a tie-break which he lost 7-3.
"Now I must play matches to try to regain my confidence," Muster said.

Sampras's demise was much more predictable. He was meeting a player who was ranked in the top 10 two years ago and was short of match practice, having had to pull out of tournaments in Hong Kong and Tokyo earlier this month with tendinitis.
His past record in Monte Carlo has been far from impressive. He has never won a match here and was forced out with a twisted ankle two years ago.

Hopes that Sampras would fare better on Tuesday were raised by an impressive first set during which he served and volleyed perfectly. But his game fell apart from then on and Larsson passed him almost at will.
"I watched Becker and Muster losing on television and I told myself it was promising," Larsson, now ranked 43rd in the world, said. "The court was very heavy which suited me fine."
After complaining about the cold weather in the principality, Sampras said: "Obviously I need matches on clay right now. Now I'm heading back to America for two weeks then coming back for Rome."
Becker, like Sampras back on clay for the first time in a season so far marred by injury, made a promising start against Furlan but also had difficulty adapting to the slow surface.
Currently ranked 12th in the world, the German resumed playing only last week in Tokyo after a two-month break because of a tendinitis. He had also complained of thigh pains in Tokyo.
"It's a big disappointment because I was so close to winning but to be so close to win when I served so poorly was a surprise," said Becker.
